p: Now there is at Jerusalem by: There is no disease so old which Christ cannot heal.
pool: Of which cattle drank, and used to be plunged in, since there was a great abundance of water at Jerusalem.
Bethesda: That is to say, the house of pouring out, because a great abundance of water was poured out into that place.
The Jews therefore said unto him: True religion is assaulted most cruelly by the pretence of religion itself.

But Jesus answered them: The work of God was never the breach of the sabbath, and the works of Christ are the works of the Father, both because they are one God, and also because the Father does not work except in the Son.

his Father: That is, his alone and no one else's, which they gather from his saying, "And I work", applying this word "work" to himself which properly belongs to God, and therefore makes himself equal to God.
of himself: Not only without his Father's authority, but also without his mighty working and power.

seeth the Father do: This must be understood of the person of Christ, which consists of two natures, and not simply of his Godhead: so then he says that his Father moves and governs him in all things, but yet nonetheless, when he says he works with his Father, he confirms his Godhead.

likewise: In like sort, jointly and together. Not because the Father does some things, and then the Son works after him and does the same, but because the might and power of the Father and the Son work equally and jointly together.
For as the Father raiseth up: The Father makes no man partaker of everlasting life except in Christ, in whom alone also he is truly worshipped.
judgeth: This word "judgeth" is taken by the figure of speech synecdoche to represent all governing.

no man: These words are not to be taken as though they simply denied that God governed the world, but rather they deny that he governed as the Jews imagined it, who separate the Father from the Son, whereas indeed, the Father does not govern the world, but only in the person of his Son, being made manifest in the flesh: so he says below in Joh 5:30, that he came not to do his own will: that his doctrine is not his own, that the blind man and his parents did not sin Joh 7:16; Joh 9:3, etc.
Verily: The Father is not worshipped except by his Son's word apprehended by faith, which is the only way that leads to eternal life.
Verily: We are all dead in sin and cannot be made alive by any other means, except by the word of Christ apprehended by faith.
authority to execute judgment also: That is, high and sovereign power to rule and govern all things, in so much that he has power over life and death.
the Son of man: That is, he will not only judge the world as he is God, but also as he is man, he received this from his Father, to be judge of the world.
Marvel not at this: All will eventually appear before the judgment seat of Christ to be judged.
And shall come: Faith and infidelity will be judged by their fruits.
forth: From their graves.
resurrection of life: To that resurrection which has everlasting life following it: against which is set the resurrection of condemnation, that is, which is followed by condemnation.
I can: The Father is the author and approver of all things which Christ does.
of mine own self do nothing: See above in Joh 5:22.
as I hear: As my Father directs me, who dwells in me.
true: Faithful, that is, worthy to be credited; see Joh 8:14.

Ye sent unto John: Christ is declared to be the only Saviour by John's voice, and infinite miracles, and by the testimonies of all the prophets. But the world, being addicted to false prophets, and desirous to seem religious, does not see any of these things.
a season to rejoice in his: A little while.
love of God in you: Love toward God.
Do not think that I will: This denial does not set aside that which is said here, but corrects it, as if Christ said, the most severe accuser the Jews will have is Moses, not him.
